sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law-based corporation statutes, US-inspired commercial law, constitutional supreme law, and customary land law overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States, as amended 2003
Pacific Island Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA), under the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus), in force 2020

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Business Corporations Act, 1990 (Marshall Islands Revised Code, Title 25), as amended; the Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Act, 2012 (MIRC Title 26), as amended; the Financial Intelligence Unit establishment statutes and AML/CFT directives issued by the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit; the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Rules applicable to registered non-resident business corporations and maintained by licensed registered agents under the Business Corporations Act.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing from the beneficial owner's domestic corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or Companies House in the owner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if origin jurisdiction is an HCCH Apostille Convention member) OR Consular Legalization (if origin jurisdiction is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or registered agent of the parent or proposed shareholder entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Ultimate Beneficial Ownership declaration and certified passport copies of all individuals holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from a regulated commercial bank confirming KYC/AML status and source of funds of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated bank or licensed finance institution in the entity's principal banking jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; if neither available, original notarized bank letter with bank seal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to Act as Registered Agent and Registered Office, addressed to the Registrar of Corporations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original signed instrument; notarization accepted, apostille/consular legalization not required for internal filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the UK/EU consolidated sanctions lists, and the Marshall Islands domestic sanctions and prohibited-persons registry. Enhanced due diligence is required for any Politically Exposed Person or family member/close associate of a PEP, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification before incorporation. Negative screening results must be documented in the registered agent's AML file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations Online Name Clearance and Registry Portal (Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands), accessible through licensed registered agents under the Business Corporations Act, 1990
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in the English/Latin script using the 26 letters A-Z without special diacritics; Marshallese or other language names are transliterated into phonetically equivalent Latin script. The name must include a mandatory corporate suffix such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or 'Company' or an approved abbreviation thereof. Names using Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, or other non-Latin scripts are not accepted unless transliterated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A successfully cleared name is reserved for 30 calendar days and is non-extendable by law. If rejected, the Registrar issues a written refusal citing the statutory or administrative ground. The applicant or its licensed registered agent may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days of refusal, attaching a formal written submission, supporting legal authorities, and up to three alternative names. The Registrar must issue a reconsideration decision within 21 business days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of the Marshall Islands under applicable civil procedure rules.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this non-resident B2B Enterprise SaaS structure. The entity must maintain a registered office in the Marshall Islands through a licensed registered agent, including a physical street address for service of process. The business itself may operate entirely from offshore with no local employees or operational premises; the tax-exempt non-resident status does not require a physical commercial office in the Marshall Islands.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified regulatory risk under 5% for a standard low-risk B2B SaaS entity with no local operations and licensed registered agent compliance. Unannounced on-site inspections are possible only on the registered agent's premises and generally occur in response to an AML/CFT audit trigger, beneficial ownership non-compliance suspicion, or an international information exchange request; remote operations of the beneficial owner are not routine inspection targets.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and statutory name reservation fee
Business Corporation non-resident incorporation filing fee
Licensed registered agent and registered office fee (first year)
Beneficial ownership register setup, record-keeping, and UBO filing (first year)
Certificate of Good Standing and certified corporate extracts
Apostille or consular legalization of corporate due diligence documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI consular/authentication service or home-jurisdiction competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic sanctions screening per UBO/director
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent / AML compliance vendor

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Independent pre-incorporation legal due diligence opinion

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, 1990 (as amended), Title 51 of the Marshall Islands Revised Statutes, Division 1; principal sections include 51 MIRC §14 (Articles of Incorporation), §15 (Corporate name requirements), §16 (By-laws), §20 (Issuance of shares) and §25 (Registered agent and registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands; for non-resident corporations, filing administration is channeled through International Registries, Inc. (IRI) as the official worldwide agency of the Marshall Islands Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation for a Non-Resident Business Corporation, together with the registered agent's acceptance of appointment.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a Non-Resident Business Corporation; shares may be authorized with or without par value, and no escrow account, bank attestation, or capital deposit obligation applies at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board approves the subscription and issuance of 10,000,000 common shares, no par value, to the subscribers at a stated consideration of US$0.001 per share, payment of which is hereby acknowledged; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be the registered agent's address as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the agent's written acceptance is approved; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, respectively, to serve at the pleasure of the Board; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts and execute all customary corporate instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry; submissions are accepted digitally through the IRI online client portal or by email via the IRI filing office in Reston, Virginia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request listing three alternative corporate names in descending order of preference, together with a declaration that the preferred name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not contain restricted words such as 'Bank', 'Trust', or 'Insurance' absent special consent. The Registry reserves the approved name for 30 days, within which the Articles of Incorporation must be filed.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form or written letter
Copy of the incorporator's valid passport
Draft Articles of Incorporation (name block only)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or conflicts with an existing name, the Registry issues a deficiency note identifying the conflict; the applicant may select an alternative name from the submitted priority list or file a fresh reservation request, which is processed without additional Registry penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution, and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the incorporator's jurisdiction and the IRI-approved registered agent for the Marshall Islands.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in English stating the corporate name, the registered agent's name and Majuro address, the registered office address, a broad purpose clause expressly authorizing software development, cloud services and B2B SaaS licensing, the authorized share structure, and the incorporator's identity. The incorporator executes the articles before a notary public; the registered agent signs a separate acceptance of appointment. The notarized original is retained in the corporate minute book and a scanned execution copy is transmitted for filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation signed by the incorporator
Registered agent's acceptance of appointment
Statement of authorized share capital and par value designations
Certified copy of the incorporator's identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries execution or notarization formalities, the applicant may cure the deficiency by re-executing the Articles before a notary whose signature is apostilled under the Hague Convention, or by submitting a corrected signature page; the filing timeline is extended by the period of the deficiency notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Articles of Incorporation and Payment of State Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, acting through the IRI filing office in Reston, Virginia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the completed Articles of Incorporation package to the IRI filing office together with payment of the US$450 state incorporation fee by wire transfer to the Marshall Islands Registry account or through the IRI approved billing arrangement. The filing is endorsed by the Registrar and the entity comes into existence as of the endorsement date and time.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (full package)
Proof of payment or fee remittance advice
Name reservation certificate
Registered agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for substantive defects, the Registrar issues a Notice of Deficiency; the applicant has 14 calendar days to respond through the registered agent, and corrected pages may be resubmitted without payment of a new fee if the entity is not yet deemed incorporated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Charter Document Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon endorsement, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of the legal existence of the Business Corporation. The registered agent delivers a certified charter package containing the Certificate of Incorporation, endorsed Articles, by-laws templates, share certificate specimens, and the corporate minute book to the beneficial owner or its counsel.
required_dossiers: Endorsed Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate minute book and share certificate templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains typographical or legal errors, the registered agent may file a Certificate of Correction under 51 MIRC; purely typographical corrections are accepted without re-notarization or additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of By-laws and First Organizational Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Business Corporation; internal governance matter not filed with the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the by-laws and execute the pro-forma First Board Resolution, either at a physical organizational meeting or, more commonly, by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting. The board ratifies the share subscription, issues share certificates to the subscriber list, designates the registered agent's address as the registered office, appoints the first officers, and authorizes the opening of bank and payment service provider accounts for B2B SaaS operations.
required_dossiers: Organizational consent or minutes of the first board meeting
Share ledger and issued share certificates
By-laws adopted by the board
Registered office and agent acceptance records
Bank account opening resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in organizational formalities are cured by executing a subsequent unanimous written consent ratifying all prior board actions; the by-laws may include a ratification clause to validate any omitted procedural step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Registration Fee Compliance and Registered Agent Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations and the IRI corporate services administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the annual government fee of US$400 for the non-resident Business Corporation on or before the day 30 days preceding each anniversary of incorporation, and file the biennial statement confirming the directors, officers, registered agent, and registered office address. Any change of registered agent or registered office is effected by a single Change of Registered Agent filing.
required_dossiers: Annual fee payment instruction or wire confirmation
Biennial officer and director statement
Change of Registered Agent form (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late payment may trigger administrative dissolution and a reinstatement penalty; the corporation may apply for reinstatement within 12 months of dissolution by paying all arrears, applicable penalties, and the reinstatement fee under the revival procedure of 51 MIRC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (for non-resident corporate status) and Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMIEPA); no industrial licensing board mandate applies because the entity operates as a non-resident digital service provider with no physical manufacturing facility or local place of business in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no industrial operating permit, manufacturing license, or local business license is required for a Non-Resident Business Corporation engaged exclusively in enterprise B2B SaaS software development, cloud licensing, and related digital services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — enterprise cloud software development and SaaS subscription licensing are not listed as prescribed undertakings under the Environmental Protection Act 1999; no full EIA report, preliminary screening, or registration certificate is triggered absent a physical data center, office installation, or other regulated facility in the RMI.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, air emission, or solid waste discharge points exist at the corporate entity level for this purely non-resident digital service operation. Should the company later establish a physical office or data center in the RMI, the facility would be required to comply with RMIEPA Clean Water and Air Quality Regulations, including zero untreated discharge to lagoon waters, VOC emission limits for stationary combustion sources, and use of RMIEPA-licensed waste disposal contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not triggered for a non-resident entity with no physical premises in the Marshall Islands. If a local office were opened in Majuro, the company would be required to obtain fire safety certification under the RMI Fire Prevention Code, structural load inspection and occupancy clearance from the Building Inspectorate, and workplace registration under the Occupational Health and Safety Act prior to occupation; none of these clearances applies to the currently contemplated virtual, non-resident B2B SaaS operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Administration (RCA), Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; official government portal: https://rmi.gov.mh
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Non-Resident Business Corporation: (1) file Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, including a declaration that the corporation will not carry on business in the Marshall Islands; (2) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation; (3) if the corporation later derives Marshall Islands-source income, apply to the RCA on Form TIN-01 with the certificate, registered agent details and local business license; (4) no VAT ID is available because the RMI has no VAT/GST system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Non-resident status is elected at incorporation under the Business Corporations Act; a corporation making this election is exempt from income tax and gross revenue tax on offshore income. The RMI has no check-the-box classification and no hybrid mismatch election; no US-style entity classification election is recognised.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None (RMI levies no VAT/GST or sales and use tax; customs duties apply only to imported physical goods)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – no VAT/GST registration threshold exists in the RMI (economy uses USD)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI does not mandate e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-based transmission to the RCA, or digital stamping for indirect tax purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in the VAT sense because the RMI has no VAT/GST. Cross-border B2B enterprise SaaS supplied by a Non-Resident Business Corporation to foreign customers falls outside the RMI territorial tax net. To maintain the exemption the corporation must not (i) carry on business in the RMI, (ii) derive Marshall Islands-source income, or (iii) hold real property in the RMI. No export registration or zero-rating approval is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: No mandatory customs documentation bundle exists for offshore SaaS exports; electronic software delivery involves no customs export declaration. If physical media is ever shipped, an RMI Customs Export Declaration and bill of lading may be required, but no VAT refund will arise.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no export VAT zero-rating or refund regime in the RMI, therefore no clawback of VAT refunds is possible. Nonetheless, abusive claims of non-resident exemption where the corporation in fact earns Marshall Islands-source income will trigger RCA reassessment, interest at 1.5% per month, late payment penalties of up to 10% per month (capped at 50% of the tax due), and criminal fines of up to USD 10,000 or imprisonment under the Income Tax Act. False customs export declarations may attract forfeiture and fines up to three times the goods' value under the Customs Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No standalone RMI central bank or foreign exchange administration exists. Banking supervision and licensing are administered by the Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands. The de facto monetary authority is the U.S. Federal Reserve because the U.S. dollar is legal tender under the Compact of Free Association.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender, giving the RMI a fully dollarized, fully convertible monetary system. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible, with no foreign-exchange controls, no repatriation permits, and no profit-remittance taxation or FX surcharge. Practical hurdles are limited to documentary compliance by the paying and receiving banks, including U.S. OFAC sanctions screening and internal AML/KYC policies. A non-resident Business Corporation may hold funds, pay dividends, and remit liquidation proceeds in USD without central-bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The RMI imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no export- proceeds surrender obligation because exports and all commercial receipts are denominated in U.S. dollars, the domestic currency. Foreign-currency export proceeds, if any, may be held or converted freely without obligation to the RMI government or to any monetary authority.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low–Medium as a business matter, and legally constrained. The RMI Banking Act 1991 and the Financial Institutions (Financial Obligations) Regulations 2001 require any deposit-taking or custodial banking activity to be licensed by the Banking Commissioner; there is no standalone e-money institution (EMI) or digital-bank licensing regime. Offshore digital EMIs, including Wise B2B and Stripe Billing, cannot lawfully open virtual accounts in the RMI as principal bank substitutes. However, they may be engaged lawfully as payment facilitators that route funds to and from a licensed RMI bank account, provided the underlying customer account is held at Bank of Marshall Islands, Inc. or Bank of Guam (Marshall Islands Branch). The RMI entity must maintain a licensed-USD bank account as the liquidity anchor; otherwise, external payment processors will reject onboarding or treat the RMI entity as unbankable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in substance. RMI licensed banks generally require a corporate representative and at least one beneficial owner or authorized signatory with 25%+ ownership to attend an initial face-to-face KYC interview, either at a Majuro branch or at a recognized overseas correspondent location. Pure remote account opening is not generally available to non-resident Business Corporations. A video interview may be accepted for ancillary signatories, but initial onboarding for a non-resident entity commonly requires either physical attendance or a notarized, embassy-certified interview package, including original board resolutions, passport pages, address proof, and corporate registers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident legal entity with registered-agent address and no physical office in RMI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Articles/Bylaws, Certificate of Good Standing, registered-agent certificate, beneficial-ownership register, lease or virtual-office agreement in Majuro, board resolution appointing local registered agent, and a substance narrative showing operational management outside RMI.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt status and absence of local corporate tax filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RMI certificate of tax exemption, director's declaration of non-resident nature, legal opinion from qualified RMI counsel confirming no domestic tax liability, audited financial statements (prepared under IFRS or US GAAP) proving foreign-source activities, and clear nexus documentation for SaaS licensing outside RMI.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-heavy B2B SaaS revenue with cross-border software licenses and recurring charges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed enterprise SaaS contracts, customer invoices, payment processor settlement statements, software license terms, IP ownership registry, uptime/service evidence, and commercial model description consistent with ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth questionnaire, shareholder bank statements for at least 6 months, audited financials or payslips covering the funding period, board resolution authorizing capitalization, subscription documents, and a signed declaration of lawful funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership layering through offshore trusts, holdings, or nominees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership register for all natural persons owning or controlling 25% or more, notarized entity chart, trust deeds or nominee declarations, passport copies and proof of address for all UBOs, and independent sanctions/PEP screening clearance reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Stripe_Billing and Wise_B2B as third-party payment rails causing transaction layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed payment-facilitator agreements, merchant account identifiers, flow charts showing fund routing from SaaS customers to processor to RMI bank account, sample clearing statements, and a monitoring procedure for identifying unusual transaction velocity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound USD capital injections for a non-resident Business Corporation are cleared through the U.S. banking network, primarily via SWIFT MT103 or Fedwire. The injector wires USD to the RMI bank's U.S. correspondent, which posts the funds to the beneficiary account at Bank of Marshall Islands, Inc. or Bank of Guam (Marshall Islands Branch). The RMI has no central-bank purpose-code regime; banks instead rely on the wire's 'remittance information' field. Compliant instructions must include: a) beneficiary bank SWIFT/BIC; b) full beneficiary name as per incorporation; c) RMI account number; d) an explicit purpose line such as 'Equity contribution – Business Corporation capital'; and e) OFAC-compliant originator details. Verification requires submission of the capitalization board resolution, share issuance calculation, source-of-funds evidence, and a completed UBO declaration before unconditional crediting. Capital escrow accounts may be used temporarily to allow bank counsel to verify the injection before transfer to the operating account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for general vendor payments, SaaS licensing fees, subcontractor payments, and operational expenditures. For high-value procurement of hardware, managed infrastructure, or services requiring documentary credit, a Commercial Letter of Credit via SWIFT MT700 is permissible. Because the RMI does not operate a domestic RTGS system, USD payments are cleared through the U.S. correspondent network, CHIPS, Fedwire, or ACH/RTP for lower-value items. Every outbound MT103 must include a valid BIC, the beneficiary bank's account, and an appropriate U.S.-destination clearing path; all wires are parsed against OFAC sanctions. For recurring SaaS payouts and processor settlements, standard daily or weekly crypto-like settlement is not available; the RMI account receives aggregated USD settlement directly from Stripe/Wise, then authorizes MT103 payments to the operating vendor set.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla currency forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/AUD, USD/JPY) executed with a licensed international bank or correspondent bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid or restricted emerging-market currencies where physical delivery is impractical
Cross-currency swaps (legally covered by ISDA) for long-term balance-sheet hedging of non-USD SaaS revenue or vendor liabilities
Plain-vanilla FX options and collars purchased from a licensed bank for cash-flow protection without leverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (statutory annual return of corporate details)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands Company Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the calendar month in which the anniversary of incorporation occurs; e.g., a corporation incorporated on 15 June is required to file by 30 June of each subsequent calendar year. No statutory grace period applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty of USD 100 is assessed if the Annual Report is not filed by the last day of the anniversary month. The corporation loses 'good standing' certification, which impairs its ability to obtain certificates of good standing, transfer ownership, or complete commercial transactions. If the report remains unfiled for twelve months past the due date, the Registrar may administratively strike the corporation from the register, terminating its separate legal existence and limited liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confidential Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation and UBO Return Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations (Confidential UBO Database), Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial beneficial ownership report must be filed within 60 days of incorporation. Annual re-confirmation is integrated with the Annual Report and due by the last day of the anniversary month. Any change in beneficial ownership, including changes arising from shareholding transfers, must be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate government fee is levied for the UBO return; non-compliance is addressed through the Annual Report late fee of USD 100 and penalties under the Beneficial Ownership Regulations 2021. Persistent failure to file, update, or confirm beneficial ownership constitutes a statutory offense subject to monetary fines and corrective orders by the Registrar, and may result in withholding of the certificate of good standing or administrative strike-off in cases of serious or repeated default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a non-resident domestic Business Corporation under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act 1990. No revenue, asset, share-capital, or employee threshold triggers a mandatory audit where the entity is privately held, not listed on a recognized securities exchange, and derives no income from sources within the Marshall Islands. An audit becomes mandatory only if the corporation is admitted to listing on a securities exchange or if its articles of incorporation, by-laws, or a binding shareholder agreement expressly imposes an independent audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Marshall Islands imposes no local statutory accounting framework on a non-resident Business Corporation. Books and records must accurately reflect financial transactions and may be maintained in US dollars. IFRS or US GAAP may be adopted as the internal financial reporting framework; no public filing of financial statements is required for a non-resident exempt corporation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended in 2020) and the Beneficial Ownership Regulations 2021, every Marshall Islands Business Corporation must (i) establish and maintain at its registered office a confidential internal Register of Beneficial Owners identifying each individual with a 25 percent or greater ownership interest, control interest, or voting right; (ii) file an initial confidential beneficial ownership report with the Registrar within 60 days of incorporation; (iii) re-confirm the accuracy of the beneficial ownership data on each Annual Report cycle; and (iv) file an updated return within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership. In the case of shareholding transfers, re-confirmation is required for any transfer that changes the identity of a 25 percent holder or alters the controlling individual; ordinary transfers below this threshold are recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the next annual confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; if voluntarily engaged for investor or banking purposes, USD 3,000 - 8,000 per annum for a small B2B SaaS entity

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) imposes no general corporate income tax under the Income Tax Act 1989 on a Business Corporation that is a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (i.e., incorporated under the Business Corporations Act 1990 but transacting no business within RMI). No CIT, no capital gains tax, no payroll tax and no branch profits tax apply.
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0%. No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions are needed, as the tax base is zero. The only governmental annual burden is the Business Corporations Act annual registration fee (franchise tax) and the foreign-owned Business License fee (RMI Business License Act 1991) — the latter applies only if the entity actually conducts domestic business; a pure non-resident B2B SaaS seller remains outside both the 3% Business Gross Revenue Tax (GRT Act 2010) and all income taxes. No tax loss carryforward exists because no assessable income concept is created for such entities.
